title: System Engineer, Graviton Team
descriptionHtml:
Annapurna Labs is the team behind AWS (Amazon Web Services) Graviton — the industry's most advanced Arm-based server CPU — and we operate like a start-up with the scale of the world's largest cloud provider.

Our Graviton System group owns the design, manufacturing, and health of the Arm-based server fleet powering Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud). We work close to the metal — across firmware, board bring-up, diagnostics, and hardware debug — to keep servers running and return failed units to production fast. In close partnership with design partners, data center operations, and hardware engineering teams, we bring new server platforms into the fleet and drive them to launch faster, healthier, and more reliably, at a scale that directly impacts millions of customers around the world.
If you are a systems, HW, or SW engineer who thrives on hard problems at the intersection of hardware and software, enjoys root-causing failures on real servers, and wants to see your work make a measurable difference across a global fleet — we would love to talk.

We're looking for a System Engineer with Software or Hardware Engineering background to be part of defining, shaping and integrating solutions to next generation of our cloud platforms.

We are looking for an exceptional engineer to own the development, testing, and monitoring of the manufacturing health of Amazon Graviton server products. You will be part of a team integrating new silicon, hardware, firmware, and software into a revolutionary system architecture.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead triage, debugging, and root cause analysis of systems in AWS data centers
• Enhance troubleshooting capabilities and drive closure of in-fleet problems
• Analyze customer workflows and requirements to provide targeted resolutions
• Collaborate with Annapurna Labs monitoring team and root cause teams to improve product quality and reliability in fleet operations
• Represent the customer voice by providing fleet operation insights and requirements to Annapurna Labs' ASIC design, software development, QA, and architecture teams
• Develop and maintain training materials, quality documentation, and collateral to improve in-fleet operations
• Design and implement tools and scripts to support projects and customize solutions based on requirements
• Travel as needed, approximately 2-4 times per year

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related fields
- Knowledge of scripting languages (bash, python, etc.)
- 8+ years of experience as System Engineer; experience working with systems, including software, firmware, and hardware components

Preferred qualifications

- Computer architecture knowledge
- High-speed interfaces knowledge and debug capabilities- PCIe, Ethernet, DDR etc.
- Experience with server (x86 / ARM) design or architecture.
- Experience with operating systems, networking, and remote debugging.

title: IT Support Associate II, Ops Tech Solutions (OTS)
descriptionHtml:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. OpsTech IT provides nonstop global IT support to Amazon Operations as a vital piece to the puzzle. We are looking for self-motivated individuals to take on new challenges and motivate teams in fostering solutions to the hurdles we face. Together, we take ownership for what we do — whether supporting IT infrastructure, developing new technology in-house, launching a new Amazon Operations facility, or delighting our customers by delivering packages directly to them.

About The Role
As an IT Support Associate II, you will use your skills to support the operations team in resolving technical problems within Amazon operations facilities in a defined geographical area that span across a multitude of technical disciplines. We are committed to improvement; you will be encouraged to participate in career development opportunities as presented to progress your career at Amazon.

What Do We Offer?
Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there’s more: we are a casual dress code at each of our locations (jeans, t-shirts, safety shoes and at times a neon safety vest will be your daily outfit). Learn more about Amazon in Andy Jassy's most recent letter to shareholders at https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/2021-letter-to-shareholders.

Key job responsibilities
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- Allocating, maintaining, and troubleshooting of IT equipment used in Amazon Operations facilities.
- Handling support requests and procedures across the network.
- Assisting in training new hires.
- Continuous learning of new technologies.
- Supporting customers from multiple buildings in the area, as well as remote customers.
- Moving up to 49lbs as well as standing and walking for shifts lasting up to 12 hours.
- Traveling within your local or regional area to support our customers.

Basic qualifications

- Experience troubleshooting integrated and interdependent computer systems
- Experience in a dynamic environment with a high degree of customer service
- Can lift up to 49 pounds, stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- 1+ years of Windows, Mac or Linux Operating systems support experience or equivalent experience

Preferred qualifications

- CompTIA A+, CompTIA Network+, Cisco/CCNA, Linux (Redhat), Microsoft hardware (installation), AWS, or other industry relevant certifications

title: Sr. Product Manager - Tech, OpsTech Solutions, OTS Delivery Software Engineering (DSE)
descriptionHtml:
Every Amazon package that ships, every grocery order that is fulfilled, and every locker that opens depends on technology our teams keep running. Amazon’s OpsTech Solutions (OTS) is the IT operations and infrastructure organization for all of Amazon Worldwide Operations including Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS), delivering reliable technology to more than one million associates and operators across every geography and all business miles. OTS is transforming from reactive support to proactive, AI-powered service delivery. The data products powering that transformation are at the center of how the organization plans, decides, and operates.

What this role is: You will own the product strategy for the OTS Data Products portfolio, spanning four data products (Nodal Efficiency, Timesheet Adherence, Scenario Planner, and Short Term Planning) and five agentic workflow products (Printer Agent, MCM Agent, CSDA, OTS MCP, and OneVoice). You decide what gets built, what gets deprecated, and how these products become one coherent, reusable portfolio. This is the role that determines whether OTS’s data investments compound or stay siloed.
This is a platform and portfolio role. You will work across two engineering organizations, ANCHOR and Delivery Software Engineering (DSE), as well as partner analytics and program teams. An emerging ecosystem of AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) services is an important part of the landscape, but your scope is the wider OTS data products estate, not any single team or service. You will define and drive the shared product strategy, standards, and access layer that these teams build on and that OTS customers consume.
Across OTS, teams have built valuable data products (forecasting services, operational metrics grounded in validated data), each proven in its own domain. The opportunity is to connect these strong point solutions across third-party platforms (ServiceNow) and in-house 1P services into one coherent portfolio, so that every new data-driven solution becomes a matter of configuration and connection rather than a net-new build. Your customers span field technicians who consume operational intelligence, program managers who configure forecasts and derive AI-driven insights, leaders who query validated metrics in natural language, and engineers who integrate with data products programmatically.

Key Highlights
• Own the product strategy and roadmap for the OTS Data Products portfolio (forecasting, science, analytics, and data tooling) across ANCHOR and Delivery Software Engineering (DSE) teams.
• Drive the reactive-to-proactive transformation by making OTS data accessible, reusable, and trustworthy through a foundational-services model: design once, deploy many.
• Shape the AI agent and MCP access layer that lets operators and leaders reach OTS data through natural-language and programmatic interfaces.
• Set the direction that multiple engineering teams build toward, backed by executive sponsorship and a clear mandate across the portfolio.
• Serve diverse customer personas across a spectrum of data latencies, from near-real-time operational needs on the front line to executive-level strategic insights.


Key job responsibilities
• Define and own a multi-year product vision and roadmap for OTS data products, unifying forecasting, science, analytics, and the AI agent and MCP ecosystem into one coherent portfolio.
• Act as the voice of the customer across OTS program teams, translating operational needs into product requirements and making disciplined trade-offs between time, effort, and feature depth.
• Partner with engineering leaders across contributing teams to shape architecture decisions, resolve overlap between services (e.g., ensuring a knowledge graph calls an existing metrics service rather than duplicating it), and drive build-vs-buy-vs-reuse decisions.
• Drive the AI agent and MCP access-layer strategy, establishing clear ownership boundaries between the common front door and supporting data services.
• Establish north-star and adoption metrics that make the foundational-services thesis measurable, and own the Monthly and Quarterly Business Review reporting standards that keep the portfolio accountable.
• Align partner engineering teams and stakeholders across competing priorities — driving adoption so teams choose to build on the shared portfolio rather than around it.
• Contribute to annual planning mechanisms (OP1/OP2) with clear, well-reasoned investment proposals, and maintain mechanisms to continuously capture voice of the customer from both internal OTS employees and operational customers.


A day in the life
Your day moves between strategy and execution. You review portfolio metrics and update roadmaps with the contributing teams, then run voice-of-the-customer sessions to make sure priorities reflect real operational pain points across personas, from a field technician relying on operational intelligence to a leader asking a natural-language question of validated metrics. You join architecture discussions to resolve how forecasting, the MCP and agent layer, and supporting data services fit together, and where boundaries between overlapping services should sit. In the afternoon, you make prioritization trade-offs with engineering leaders across teams whose roadmaps you influence but do not control, then shift to drafting strategy narratives and investment proposals for senior review.

About the team
OTS sits within Amazon’s largest support organization for Worldwide Operations, building a broader strategy to enhance support operations through technology and AI. OTS data products are how that strategy becomes actionable: forecasting and science services that help program teams plan, operational metrics grounded in validated data, and an emerging AI agent and MCP ecosystem that meets users at the point of need. The ANCHOR team is a key contributor to this landscape, delivering products such as OPAL and agentic tooling, and it partners with Delivery Software Engineering (DSE), Global Workforce Management (GWM), and the OTS and RME program teams. This role defines what the OTS data products portfolio should be across those teams; the engineering organizations deliver the how.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience working with Data & AI related technologies, including, but not limited to, AI/ML, GenAI, Analytics, Database, and/or Storage
- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
- Demonstrated ability to influence and align partner engineering teams and stakeholders across competing priorities, without direct authority.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience bridging technical and business teams to collect and refine requirements, prioritize incoming work requests, and ensure all committed work is delivered on time
- MBA
- Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions

title: Engineering Operations Technician , DCEO
descriptionHtml:
How would you like to be a part of Earth’s most customer-centric company? You would work with teams of front-line responders who support the operations of some of the world’s most Customer Centric data centers. Our Data Center Engineering Operations team maintain and operate our critical infrastructure systems so that they are prepared to stand up against any situation.

AWS has the world’s largest cloud computing portfolio. As an Amazonian you will work in some of the most sophisticated, safe, and secure data centers in the world. Our Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT’s) help keep them that way by working with the brightest minds from around the globe to help test and implement the newest technology and work practices to meet the demands of a changing market.

We have a passion for learning and evolving, it’s how we have helped define ourselves as leaders in the industry. Let’s work hard, have fun, and make history!

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule including night shift. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

About the team
This position is for back half night shift. We work Wednesday through Saturday from 6pm to 6am. There is a shift differential for night shift.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work a flexible work schedule including evenings, overnights, and weekends
- 1+ years of electrical facilities maintenance, or 1+ years of mechanical facilities

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- Associate's degree in related field, or technical degree in related field

title: Sort Center Area Manager Jr, Sort Center
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is looking for high-potential leaders, who are ready to own their impact in Amazon Operations as an entry-level manager. We promise you will have your leadership capacity stretched to its full potential. As a front-line leader, you will have an opportunity to truly invest in others and develop a people-focused leadership style, while mastering the tools, processes, and operations that have created the most customer-centric company on Earth. If you want to be involved in continuing to define the future of online retail, and are dynamic and an organized self-starter, join our team in Amazon Operations as an Area Manager Jr.
As an Area Manager Jr, you will have the opportunity to lead and develop your own team of Amazon Associates in a Sort Center environment. Your main focus will be motivating, mentoring and coaching your team. As a servant leader, the Area Manager Jr will ensure that their team of Amazon Associates have all the tools needed to succeed for any task during a shift. Engaging with your team during a shift to ensure that the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance performance and engagement are maintained are core functions of the role. Come learn how the largest online retailer in the world runs its fulfillment and delivery networks!

As Sort Center Area Manager Jr, you will be in charge of part of the operation of our work centers during an assigned shift. These operations involve the management of human, technological and physical resources to ensure the correct execution of the daily operation plan aligned with results.
Within these functions you will be mainly in charge of:
• Continuous improvement pillar: Propose, plan and execute continuous improvement strategies that seek continuous operational efficiency.
• Industrial Safety Pillar: During the shift, you are the main person in charge of safeguarding the well-being of the personnel under your charge, being directly or indirectly hired by the company.
• Pillar Talent Management: Being a Manager at Amazon is a privilege and a responsibility, as a Manager, you will be focused on hiring and developing a workforce who will become the next Amazon leaders.
• Operational Pillar: Review the operational forecast and determine productivity requirements for the operation.

title: Software Dev Engineer III, AWS Elastic Beanstalk
descriptionHtml:
AWS Elastic Beanstalk is looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer (SDE3) to help build and extend the service. Elastic Beanstalk is how developers get an application running on AWS without becoming infrastructure experts — you upload your code, and we handle capacity provisioning, load balancing, auto scaling, and application health monitoring.

Our team builds the orchestration system at the center of the service: the public API, the workflow system that provisions and mutates customer environments, the health monitoring subsystem, the eventing pipeline, and the AWS Console experience. We are also in the middle of the most significant architectural expansion in the service's history — extending Elastic Beanstalk to run on Kubernetes and EKS, while continuing to support the millions of environments already running on our classic architecture. Doing both at once, without customer disruption, is a genuinely hard distributed systems problem.

If you are someone who is passionate about building high quality services, delighting developers, and reducing the distance between "I have code" and "it's running in production," this job is for you. You will be joining a small team where an SDE3 has real design ownership from day one — you will lead design and implementation efforts on services used at AWS scale, and act as a force multiplier for the engineers around you.

title: Software Development Engineer, EC2 Instance Networking
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to build the networking infrastructure that powers every virtual machine in the world's largest cloud? Are you excited by the challenge of writing systems software that runs on millions custom networking cards across millions of hosts?

The Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) Instance Networking team builds and operates the software-defined networking stack at the heart of AWS. Our code is what makes Virtual Private Clouds (VPC) work, what enforces customer security policies, and what enables workloads to scale from a single instance to clusters of tens of thousands. Every packet that enters or leaves an EC2 instance flows through software we write, running on custom silicon designed in-house.

This work sits at the intersection of cloud infrastructure and the AI revolution. As machine learning workloads grow to unprecedented scale - training runs spanning thousands of accelerators, clusters demanding millions of network endpoints, and fabrics pushing hundreds of gigabits per second. We build the networking primitives that make these workloads possible: high-performance interfaces, low-latency data plane protocols, and scalable network virtualization that operates predictably even under heavy churn. When the world's most ambitious AI companies scale on AWS, they're relying on the software we build.

You'll write low-level systems code in C and Rust running on custom hardware in a real-time embedded environment. You'll work on network virtualization protocols, packet processing pipelines, and availability mechanisms that must perform correctly at massive scale with sub-second latency requirements. You'll solve problems that span hardware, firmware, and software, and see the direct impact of your work on customers running some of the largest and most demanding workloads in the cloud.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and implement data plane networking software on custom hardware, working across the full software lifecycle from design through deployment and operations
- Build and improve network virtualization systems that deliver VPC connectivity, security policy enforcement, and performance isolation for EC2 customers
- Investigate and resolve complex production issues across distributed embedded systems, driving root cause analysis and permanent fixes
- Collaborate with partner teams across hardware, control plane, and ML platforms to deliver end-to-end solutions

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 4+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Knowledge of system performance, memory management, and parallel computing principles
- Experience in networking, large-scale distributed systems or a related field
- Experience in Linux and Networking protocols

They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.
Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection
- This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.
Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility
Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.


A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

- 2+ years of electrical or mechanical experience

Preferred qualifications

title: SDE II, EE Experiences, Progressive Discovery and Monetization
descriptionHtml:
Everyday Essentials (EE) is a $100B+ business and one of the fastest-growing categories at Amazon — the household staples, health and personal care, grocery, and beauty products hundreds of millions of customers reorder. We're reinventing how customers discover, buy, and get more value from them, and we're looking for Software Development Engineers who want to build that future.

The EE Experiences organization builds the shopping experience for the products customers come back for most. Our charter is Progressive Discovery and Monetization: helping customers find better products for their needs, complete their baskets, and improve EE business economics — and giving the world's largest consumer brands new and effective ways to reach those customers and grow with Amazon. We build a durable, profitable business at the intersection of the two, on the surfaces customers use every day.

This is a space where the hardest problems don't have off-the-shelf answers. We're not polishing a solved product — we're inventing experiences that don't exist yet, and the decisions we make now shape a business with room to grow for years. You'll build discovery and recommendation features, brand-facing advertising surfaces, and the backend services that power them. Your work moves from whiteboard to production in front of a very large customer base, with visibility all the way to senior leadership.

We're an AI-first team, and that shows up in two ways. We use AI throughout how we build software, and we expect our engineers to keep learning and applying the latest tools to move faster and raise the quality bar. AI is also at the core of what we build — the intelligence that helps customers find the right product is a modeling and engineering problem we work on hand in hand with scientists. If you're curious about AI, learn quickly, and like using it to solve real customer problems while keeping a clear head about where it helps and where it doesn't, you'll fit right in.

Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and own software end to end — from customer research through design, code, testing, deployment, and production operations.
Take on ambiguous problems where the goal is clear but the path is not, bring clarity, and deliver simple solutions that improve how customers find and buy everyday essentials.
Partner closely with scientists, product managers, and designers to turn customer and brand problems into products that ship worldwide.
Use generative AI tools and modern engineering practices to raise quality and velocity, and coach teammates on getting the most from them.
Own operational health for your services — monitor metrics, drive root-cause fixes, and keep improving the experience for customers and brand partners.
Raise the technical bar through code reviews, mentoring, and hiring for the best talent.

A day in the life
Most days start with the customer problem in front of you: how to help someone find better everyday-essentials products faster, or how to give brands a more effective way to reach shoppers or how to improve the profitability of the business. You dig into data, sketch a design, and talk it through with product managers and scientists before writing any code. By the afternoon you might be prototyping an idea that didn't exist yesterday, reviewing a teammate's change, or debugging something in production. Because so much here is new, you won't just pick up tickets. You'll help decide what to build, push for the approach you believe in, and see your work reach customers in weeks, not quarters.

About the team
Our team owns how customers discover and buy the everyday essentials they rely on — and how the brands behind those products reach them. Our mission is to make restocking the things you need effortless, help customers find better options and to improve the business economics along the way. Day to day you'll work with fellow engineers and partner closely with product managers, designers, and scientists, who bring the customer and data insight that shapes what we build. We're a small, fast-moving group solving open-ended problems for hundreds of millions of shoppers — a place where you own problems end to end and your ideas reach customers fast.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Experience building complex software systems that have been successfully delivered to customers
- Experience debugging, profiling, and implementing best software engineering practices in large-scale systems

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Amazon Leo Partner Services
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

As a Senior Technical Program Manager on the Amazon Leo Partner Services (ALPS) team, you will own and drive complex, externally facing technical integration programs with Amazon Leo's global distribution partners. You will serve as the primary program leader responsible for ensuring partners successfully integrate, validate, and launch satellite internet service in their contracted territories and channels. This role sits at the center of partner-facing execution and internal product coordination, spanning API onboarding, BSS/OSS integration, network readiness, operational enablement, and launch milestones. You will work cross-functionally with Amazon Leo engineering, product, solutions architecture, and operations teams to ensure partner-facing deliverables are defined, prioritized, and delivered on time.

This position may require access to export-controlled information (ECI) subject to EAR and ITAR. Final employment decision is contingent upon satisfactory completion of export control screenings and obtaining any necessary export licenses or approvals, based on nationality, citizenship, and other factors considered by applicable export control regulations

Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end partner technical integration programs from discovery through launch readiness, defining integration scope, success criteria, milestones, and deliverables across partner and Amazon Leo teams while identifying risks, dependencies, and critical path items early to drive mitigation plans.
- Lead recurring program reviews, executive checkpoints, and milestone tracking sessions with strategic distribution partners, translating partner integration requirements into clear internal execution plans and managing blockers through timely escalation.
- Coordinate delivery across multiple internal workstreams — including API releases, backend services, hardware readiness, and operational tooling — partnering with Product, Engineering, Solutions Architects, and Operations teams to align roadmaps with partner launch commitments.
- Develop and maintain standardized program artifacts such as integration plans, dependency maps, and executive status reporting, and implement repeatable frameworks for global partner onboarding and launch readiness.
- Analyze program data, track integration maturity metrics, and report launch risk to senior leadership, using insights to drive continuous improvement of the ALPS launch model and influence prioritization of partner-critical capabilities.

A day in the life
You will operate in a regional context, supporting distribution partners across Turkey and the surrounding region in coordination with central ALPS teammates and other regional TPMs. Your day may include leading a partner integration review in the morning, aligning with engineering on API readiness in the afternoon, and preparing an executive launch risk update for leadership.

Amazon Leo is a rapidly evolving organization with startup energy and global ambition. The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, builds structure where none exists, and balances deep technical understanding with disciplined program execution.

About the team
The Amazon Leo Partner Services (ALPS) team is responsible for the onboarding, integration, and enablement of Amazon Leo's distribution partners worldwide. We work with telecom operators and regional service providers to deliver satellite internet service in diverse regulatory and operational environments.

Our mission is to make Amazon Leo partnerships predictable, scalable, and launch-ready through technical rigor and disciplined program execution.

- Technical program management experience
- Experience working directly with software engineering teams
- Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

- Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

title: Principal Software Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon S3 holds the world's data. Customers of every size build on it because it gives them durability, scale, and control they can rely on, and because the controls around their data are as much a part of the product as the storage itself. Every request to S3 carries an authorization decision, made in line, at S3's request rate, within a latency budget measured in a small fraction of the request. That combination of scale, precision, and speed makes security in S3 one of the most interesting distributed systems problems at AWS.

We are building S3 for the next kind of usage. AI agents are becoming primary consumers of enterprise data, and they reach for data in patterns, at volumes, and on behalf of identities that look different from the applications and people S3 serves today. We want customers to find the security model simpler and more capable as that shift happens, and to be able to say yes to new uses of their data with confidence. Leading that work is what this role is for.

We are looking for a Principal Engineer to lead the technical direction for security in the Amazon S3 API and Request Processing organization. This organization owns the S3 API surface and the front end of the request path, which makes it the place where every access decision is made. This is a customer-facing security role: you will shape how access to S3 data is expressed by customers, evaluated on the request path, and understood by the people who are accountable for it. You will work across S3 and with partner teams in identity, analytics, and AI, and your designs will be adopted by teams broadly.

The same request path carries S3's performance, availability, and the simplicity of the API itself, and these properties are designed together rather than separately: an access decision that is elegant but slow is not a good design, and an API that is fast but hard to reason about is not either. A Principal Engineer in this organization is expected to shape the request path as a whole and to grow their scope over time, in S3 and beyond it.

Key job responsibilities
Authorization on the request path. Lead the architecture of how access decisions are modeled and evaluated in line with every S3 request. This spans the policy surfaces customers work with, the evaluation and caching that keep those decisions fast at S3 scale, and a model that stays clear and predictable for customers as S3 continues to grow.

A security model customers find easy to reason about. Make the secure path the straightforward one: fewer independent things for a customer to get right, a clear relationship between access to data and access to keys, and controls a customer can explain to their auditors with confidence.

The request path more broadly. Bring the same depth to the other properties the API and request path deliver, including latency, availability, and the design of the API surface customers and AWS services build against, so that security is designed as part of the system rather than layered onto it.

Technical leadership across the organization. Set the standard for how a large engineering organization reasons about security in design reviews and threat models, act as a technical leader on problems well outside your immediate focus, and grow the senior engineers who will raise that bar alongside you.

About the team
The S3 API and Request Processing organization owns the API that customers and AWS services use to reach their data, and the front end of the path that serves every request. It is a high-scale, high-availability systems organization, and it is where the properties customers most associate with S3 are delivered on each call. The team works closely with partners across storage, identity, analytics, and AI, and its work is visible in the daily experience of nearly every AWS customer.

Basic qualifications

- Deep experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems in production
- Depth in at least one security domain relevant to this role, such as authorization and access control, identity, or applied cryptography, and the appetite to build depth in the others
- Experience owning components where correctness, latency, and availability all matter at once
- A track record of technical leadership spanning multiple teams, including designs that other teams adopted
- Experience mentoring and growing senior engineers
- Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to move between a design review with engineers and a briefing with senior executives

Preferred qualifications

- Experience designing authorization systems evaluated on the request path under a strict latency budget
- Experience with high-throughput, low-latency request serving systems
- Experience with policy languages, formal methods, or automated reasoning applied to access control
- Experience with key management and encryption at scale
- Experience with data lake or analytics security: fine-grained access control, row and column level security, or catalog-based governance
- Experience creating architectural vision and influencing groups well beyond your own organization
- Experience representing a technical strategy directly to enterprise customers and their security and compliance teams

title: Mechanical / Electrical Engineer, InfraOps DCEO
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon is seeking a collaborative electrical maintenance professional for our Amazon Web Services Team.
This engineering operations technician position serves as the on-site maintenance technician and operator for an AWS data centre.
The Data Centre Engineering Operations Technician (EOT) is responsible for operating and maintaining all electrical, mechanical, emergency generator, and fire/life safety equipment within the data centre. The EOT serves as a technical resource to support Amazon within its data centres. Data centre equipment that supports mission-critical servers must maintain better than 99.999% uptime. EOT’s are also tasked with driving innovation while reducing operational costs in the facilities.

EOT’s are Amazon’s front line responders for hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operation. This equipment includes, but is not limited to, stand-by diesel generators, switchboards/switch-gears, UPS’s, PDU’s, AHU’s, pumps, motors, VFD’s, and building automation systems. This role will not require shift work.

Responsibilities:
- Operate and maintain mechanical and electrical equipment
- Troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal SLAs
- Perform limited maintenance tasks to include: filter changes, HVAC PMs, rack power installs, rack PDU, and rack ATS replacements
- Provide support to Data Centre Operations technicians
- Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures
- Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to while performing work
- Take daily operational readings of all mechanical and electrical equipment through routine rounds/log taking (temperatures, voltages, currents, etc.)
- Utilise internal CMMS to manage building workflows and spare part inventory
- Supervise contractors who perform servicing or preventive maintenance
- Respond to off hour emergency calls per on call rotation for any one of the region’s sites
- Fully comply with all physical security procedures and policies

descriptionHtml:
In pursuit of being Earth's Best Employer, our global Human Resources teams, known as People eXperience and Technology (PXT), drive business success by fostering a safe, inclusive, and innovative culture. The HR Business Partner is responsible for operational excellence and organizational health at assigned site(s), serving as an individual contributor partnering directly with Field Leaders and site leadership teams. You will strengthen culture and deliver business results by translating organizational priorities into actionable plans, executing business goals through data-driven decision making, and partnering with campus leaders to improve the employee experience. This role is accountable for the end-to-end employee experience, owning site-level feedback mechanisms, recognition programs, and environment standards that shape trust, engagement, and performance.
You will be expected to work onsite at an Amazon facility, supporting multiple sites within your region (campus) with regular mobility across assigned locations.


Key job responsibilities
Employee Experience & Engagement
• Foster two-way communication between employees and leaders through feedback mechanisms like Voice of the Associate, roundtables, and GEMBA walks
• Execute and monitor employee engagement strategies and recognition programs, including budget planning and employee appreciation activities
• Build an environment where employees feel safe and included, establishing Employee Resource Groups and ensuring equitable talent practices
• Maintain meaningful floor presence across the site, gathering insights and identifying early signs of disengagement

• Conduct regular site walks to assess workplace conditions and maintain facility standards in alignment with Amazon standards

• Improve site effectiveness by identifying systemic patterns, addressing root causes, and ensuring consistent, fair application of policies
Data-Driven Decision Making & Technology

• Drive adoption of HR technology solutions, AI, and self-service tools while maintaining high-touch service delivery in critical moments
Strategic PXT Leadership
• Partner with site leadership to balance operational needs with Amazon's values and people priorities
• Coach Business Leaders on effective people management practices, including performance feedback, team development, and employee relations matters
• Support change implementation by reinforcing messaging, addressing resistance, and helping leaders translate change into local routines
• Execute core PXT processes while building trust and influence through sound business acumen

Your day will be a dynamic blend of strategic thinking and data-driven decision-making. You'll leverage advanced analytics and AI-enabled tools to identify trends, anticipate business needs, and develop solutions that enhance workplace experience. From coaching leadership teams on workforce management to driving HR process excellence, you'll collaborate with Field leaders on operational objectives and team effectiveness. You'll maintain strong floor presence, building partnerships across all levels while contributing to meaningful workplace improvements through site walks, employee feedback sessions, and strategic initiatives.
Success comes from your ability to navigate organizational dynamics, lead change initiatives, and make high-judgment decisions in ambiguous situations. Through business acumen, data-driven insights, and strategic partnerships, you'll help create a workplace culture where employees feel valued and empowered.

As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.


Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment

title: Power Systems Engineer TIPM, Global Energy, sustainability, and Automation
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Power Systems Engineer to support electrical reliability, safety, and regulatory programs across Amazon's North American operations network. This role will be responsible for managing the five-year arc flash study refresh program, performing technical quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) of power system studies using SKM Power*Tools, and managing the electrical Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) program across North American facilities.
This position requires a strong understanding of industrial MV and LV power distribution systems. The successful candidate will combine technical engineering expertise with program management capabilities to improve electrical system reliability, reduce operational risks, and maintain electrical safety standards across a large portfolio of operating facilities.
This role requires 50% or more travel to operational facilities across North America to perform technical assessments, investigate equipment reliability issues, validate engineering studies, and support electrical safety program implementation.


Key job responsibilities
Arc Flash Study Refresh Program

- Manage the five-year arc flash study refresh program across North American facilities, ensuring timely completion and alignment with applicable electrical safety standards - across 200+ facilities annually.
- Maintain study inventories, track refresh schedules, and prioritize facilities based on electrical system changes, risk, and program requirements.

- Coordinate with third-party engineering firms and site teams to collect and validate electrical system data.

- Review study deliverables, identify deficiencies and NEC violations, propose appropriate cost-effective resolutions, and track corrective actions through closure, including arc flash labeling, relay/breaker settings adjustment, equipment replacement, and documentation updates.

- Establish program performance metrics and reporting to track study completion, deficiencies, and overall program health.

- Perform root cause analysis (RCA) and develop corrective and preventive actions to address equipment failures and recurring reliability concerns.

- Investigate electrical equipment failures, recurring faults, protective device misoperations, and power distribution system reliability issues.

Power Systems Studies and Technical QA/QC

- Perform detailed technical QA/QC of power system studies using SKM Power*Tools, including short-circuit, protective device coordination, arc flash, and load flow analyses.

- Independently review and validate SKM models, study assumptions, equipment parameters, protective device settings, and engineering calculations.

- Identify modeling errors, inconsistencies, and technical deficiencies in studies submitted by external engineering consultants.

- Verify study results against applicable IEEE, NFPA, and other relevant engineering standards.

- Review engineering recommendations related to protective device coordination, incident energy reduction, equipment ratings, and electrical system reliability.

- Document QA/QC findings, coordinate corrections with engineering consultants, and verify resolution before accepting final study deliverables.

- Develop and maintain standardized study review checklists, technical acceptance criteria, and QA/QC processes.

Electrical Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Program

- Manage the North American electrical LOTO program, including technical standards, implementation oversight, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement.

- Develop, maintain, and standardize electrical energy control requirements and procedures across operational facilities.

- Review electrical isolation procedures, equipment-specific energy control requirements, and single-line diagrams to ensure technically sound isolation practices.

- Partner with site maintenance teams and Workplace Health & Safety to implement program requirements, identify gaps, and drive corrective actions.

- Establish and monitor program performance metrics, audit findings, and corrective action closure.

- Provide technical guidance on electrical energy isolation, verification of absence of voltage, and safe electrical work practices.

- Coordinate periodic program reviews, procedural updates, and technical training requirements.

Electrical Reliability Engineering

- Provide electrical reliability engineering support for operating facilities, focusing on improving equipment performance, reducing unplanned downtime, and mitigating electrical system risks.

- Evaluate electrical equipment condition, maintenance practices, and failure trends to identify opportunities for reliability improvements.

- Support the development and optimization of preventive and condition-based maintenance strategies for electrical distribution equipment.

- Partner with site maintenance and operations teams to troubleshoot electrical system issues and implement sustainable engineering solutions.

- Provide emergency on-call support to facilities in North America.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or equivalent
- 5+ years’ experience performing power system studies (Short Circuit, Protective Device Coordination, Arc Flash) for medium-voltage and low-voltage industrial electrical distribution systems
- 3+ years of hands-on proficiency with SKM Power*Tools for Windows (PTW), including power system modeling, short-circuit analysis, breaker and relay protective device coordination, and arc flash analysis.
- Experience independently performing technical QA/QC of power system studies, including reviewing and validating SKM models and engineering results.
- Working knowledge of NFPA 70E, IEEE 1584-2018, applicable IEEE power system standards, and local electrical codes.
- Experience interpreting electrical single-line diagrams, protective device settings, and electrical equipment specifications.
- Experience managing multiple engineering projects or technical programs involving multiple stakeholders.
- Ability to travel 50% or more across North America, including frequent visits to operating facilities.

Preferred qualifications

- Professional Engineer (PE) license certification.
- Strong knowledge of MV relay
- Demonstrated expertise in medium-voltage (MV) protective relay settings, coordination, and commissioning, including proficiency in extracting and analyzing event reports for root-cause fault diagnosis.
- Hands-on electrical reliability engineering experience in an operational environment, with a strong understanding of industrial MV and LV power distribution systems, equipment failure mechanisms, preventive maintenance, and electrical troubleshooting
- Demonstrated experience troubleshooting electrical distribution systems, investigating equipment failures, performing root cause analysis, and developing reliability improvements in operating facilities.
- Experience developing preventive maintenance strategies, condition assessments, and electrical equipment lifecycle management programs.
- Experience managing or implementing electrical LOTO or electrical safety programs.
- Familiarity with OSHA electrical safety requirements, including 29 CFR 1910.147, and applicable Canadian regulatory requirements.
- Experience supporting electrical reliability and safety programs across multiple operational facilities.
- Strong analytical, technical writing, and stakeholder management skills.

title: Sr. Engagement Manager, Professional Services, AWS Industries
descriptionHtml:
The AWS Professional Services (ProServe) Telco, Media & Entertainment, Gaming and Sports (TMEGS) Delivery Practice is seeking a Sr. Engagement Manager (EM) to own the delivery of complex, outcome-based cloud and AI programs for our customers. In this role you are accountable for business outcomes, not just project milestones. You will help shape what we commit to, negotiate it with customer executives, and deliver it profitably.

Most of our engagements are delivered on a fixed-price, outcome-based model. You will turn customer ambitions into measurable outcomes, clear acceptance criteria and a milestone plan that both the customer and AWS can stand behind. You will work with sales and solution architects before signature to make sure what we sell is deliverable. After signature, you will manage scope, change and commercial performance with discipline: tracking earned value, protecting margin, and negotiating trade-offs with customer executives when priorities shift. You are comfortable having difficult conversations early, and you know how to protect both the customer relationship and the commercial position.

You will lead delivery teams that use AI throughout the delivery lifecycle, from requirements and design through code generation, testing and operations, to deliver outcomes faster and at higher quality than traditional approaches. You are hands-on with AI-assisted delivery tools, and fluent enough in architecture and engineering to challenge AI-generated plans and designs, make informed trade-offs on performance, security, scalability and cost, and keep quality high as delivery speed increases. You apply AWS frameworks such as Well-Architected and the Cloud Adoption Framework, and you build automated quality gates so standards hold as delivery scales.

Our largest programs combine AWS builders with AWS Partner Network (APN) partners and sometimes customer-selected system integrators. You will orchestrate this mixed workforce to a single quality bar. That means setting clear accountability, consistent acceptance criteria and mechanisms that make standards hold by design rather than by inspection. You will also drive change management on the customer side, so the organization adopts what we build and the business value is realized.

You will build trusted relationships with senior customer stakeholders up to C-level, report progress in terms of business value delivered, and spot leading indicators of risk such as velocity, environment stability, partner quality and team health, acting on them before they become escalations. As you grow, you will lead larger multi-workstream programs, help shape how we price and measure outcomes, and contribute reusable assets, patterns and AI-enabled practices that make the next engagement faster than the last. You are expected to achieve and maintain relevant AWS certifications, including in AI, and to develop deep domain expertise.

The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts that help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute enterprise cloud and AI initiatives. We provide a collection of offerings that help customers achieve specific outcomes related to enterprise cloud adoption, and focused guidance through our global specialty practices, which cover a variety of solutions, technologies and industries.


Key job responsibilities
- Owning delivery of complex, outcome-based cloud and AI programs end to end, accountable for customer business outcomes, delivery quality and commercial performance

- Managing engagement revenue and financial health: forecasting revenue against milestones, maintaining an accurate estimate at completion, driving timely milestone acceptance and billing, and identifying expansion opportunities that grow the customer relationship
- Leading delivery teams that use AI across the lifecycle (requirements, design, code generation, testing and operations), and applying enough technical depth to challenge AI-generated output and make informed trade-offs on security, performance, scalability and cost
- Orchestrating mixed teams of AWS builders, AWS Partner Network partners and customer-selected integrators to a single quality bar, with clear accountability, consistent acceptance criteria and automated quality gates
- Driving customer-side change management and adoption, so the organization realizes the value of what we build
- Reporting progress to senior stakeholders in terms of business value delivered, and acting on leading indicators of risk (velocity, environment stability, partner quality, team health) before they become escalations
- Contributing reusable assets, patterns and AI-enabled delivery practices that make each engagement faster and more repeatable than the last

title: Transportation Network Design PM, Network Design Programs
descriptionHtml:
The role can be based in Luxembourg or London.

At Amazon, we are always exploring new opportunities to shape our global business. Our Program Managers help us move forward with our best ideas and get everything in place to drive success. As you take on different projects, you’ll become an expert in our processes and see your experience evolve. Along the way, you’ll work closely with different functions across Amazon and see how working together makes us a leader in what we do.

The role will involve understanding the full transportation network connecting upstream design to downstream implementation including physical and virtual transportation processes, from our fulfillment centers on to our final mile carriers who deliver our packages to our customers. As part of the EU Network Design Programs team you will combine business process knowledge, data expertise, and influencing skills to identify and drive programs to manage change across our transportation network.

To be successful in the role, you need strong analytical skills, excellent communication skills, ability to influence across business functions and manage stakeholders’ expectations effectively. You will work in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment that requires you to be detail-oriented and comfortable in working with multiple business and technical teams.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end delivery of network design programs, from scoping through deployment and benefit measurement

- Define and manage program roadmaps aligned to the team's planning calendar, ensuring milestones land when downstream teams need them

- Govern the quality of inputs that feed network optimization models, working with data providers to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and visibility of gaps

- Translate technical model outputs into clear, actionable plans for operations and configuration teams

- Drive cross-functional alignment across operations, finance, technology, and carrier management to execute network changes

- Build and maintain mechanisms (dashboards, trackers, governance processes) that reduce reliance on manual oversight and tribal knowledge

- Identify process inefficiencies and propose structural improvements, not just incremental fixes

- Communicate program status, risks, and trade-offs to senior leadership with clarity and precision

A day in the life
No two days look the same. One morning you might be tracing why high-value network proposals were rejected and fixing the root cause before the next cycle. The next, you could be reassessing a facility constraint that just shifted and summarizing the trade-off for leadership.

Priorities change frequently. An urgent capacity issue can reprioritize your week, and you will need to judge what can wait and what cannot. The constant is that you are closing the gap between what the network should look like and what it actually looks like in production. The path there is rarely the same twice.

About the team
EU Network Design Programs is part of Amazon's Transportation Network Optimization (TNO) organization. TNO owns the full lifecycle of transportation network changes across Europe: from analytics and network modeling, through governance and validation, to deployment into Amazon's operational systems. The organization brings together network designers, analysts, engineers, and program managers working toward a shared goal.

Within TNO, our team drives the programmatic execution of optimization cycles and network transformation initiatives. We value simplicity over complexity, automation over manual effort, and outcomes over activity. Every cycle, your work moves the needle on how fast millions of customers receive their packages, and you can see it in the data the next day.

- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience in program or project management
- Experience in defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

- Experience leading process improvements

Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!
About the Role:

As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement.

You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations.

You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role.


Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
• You will perform preventative/predictive maintenance of conveyance equipment using the appropriate job plans, procedures, and manuals.

• You will conduct maintenance and basic troubleshooting of robotics and robotic work cells.

• You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all material handling equipment components.

• You will maintain and troubleshoot motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc.
• You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head

Program Requirements:
• Flexible to relocate after completion of the program

• Able to enroll in and attend a 9-week training at one of four designated training providers (Location to be determined post-interview)

• Meet the minimum qualifying score on a Mechanical Aptitude Test

Please note that while we strive to accommodate employees' preferences for shift assignments, due to operational requirements and scheduling constraints, we cannot guarantee a specific shift assignment.

Basic qualifications

- High School Diploma
- 1+ years of PC software experience including Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook experience
- vocational/technical training or an associate degree or above, or 1+ years of Amazon RME (Reliability Maintenance Engineering) experience
- Experience troubleshooting and repairing operational items
- Knowledge of mathematics
- Experience measurement reading and interpretation
- Work flexible schedules including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 4+ years of military experience
- Experience conducting predictive and preventative maintenance procedures
- Experience troubleshooting and diagnosing material handling equipment (MHE)
- Experience implementing safety standards
- Experience reading blueprints and electrical schematics

title: Software Dev Engineer, Amazon Leo Customer Terminal Software
descriptionHtml:
Project Leo is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of 3,236 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Project Leo will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.

You will design, craft, and deploy reliable embedded software for large quantity of consumer electronic products. Leo is breaking new ground with every device we design, and you will be an integral part of bringing this family of products to customers.

Key job responsibilities
· Develop embedded software for Customer Terminal devices within the Project Leo system.
· Participate in all phases of SDLC including requirements gathering, design, code, test, and code/test coverage.
· Developing embedded software in C, C++, Rust, Python or other languages
· Have experience with real-time embedded software philosophies and practices
· Have expertise with Linux and/or RTOS
· Review schematics, logic analyzer, and embedded software trouble-shooting techniques.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


A day in the life
As part of our Leo Customer Terminal Software Team, you will design and implement embedded software used in the Project Leo products. You will work in a collaborative environment with teams inside and outside of Amazon. You will craft your software from requirements, designs, code, test, to product deployment. You need to be flexible and responsive to changing priority issues.

About the team
The Leo Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect our customers to the Leo network. We provide software for both applications and the underlying Linux system. We work hand in hand with hardware, product and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
